newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: ICRC returns bodies from Afghanistan fighting.
newsitem.headline: ICRC returns bodies from Afghanistan fighting.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Tuesday it transported the bodies of 46 fighters across Afghanistan's front line into territory held by forces opposing the Taleban militia.
The transfer north of Kabul "was done without any conditions", the ICRC's Jean-Luc Paladini told reporters in the capital.
On Monday the Taleban governor of Kabul province, Mullah Khairullah Khairkhwa told journalists "80 bodies of the enemy...will be returned to the other side as a gesture of goodwill by the Taleban."
The reason for the discrepancy in numbers was not immediately apparent.
Most of the dead were victims of intense fighting following a Taleban offensive against the opposition alliance north of Kabul on December 28.
The purist Islamic Taleban, who took Kabul in September and now control more than two-thirds of the country, managed to push the opposition back some 10 km (six miles) in the two-day offensive.
When journalists visited the battlefield, dozens of bodies lay by the roadside.
Khairkhwa said there were no Taleban bodies on the other side of the front line to be retuned. He said the reason for the delay in returning the bodies was that the front line had been too active.

The Taleban face an alliance formed between the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani and northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum north of Kabul and in Afghanistan's remote northwestern provinces.
